title: Multiview Representation Learning via Distributed Joint Latent Space Structuring
abstract: arXiv:2504.18455v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study distributed multiview representation learning, a problem in which $K$ clients each observe a distinct but possibly statistically correlated view. The clients independently extract local representations from their views, which are then used by a central decoder for joint target estimation. One central difficulty is that, since the clients are not allowed to communicate with each other, they must autonomously decide what to encode. We study this coordination problem from a generalization error perspective. For both classification and regression tasks, we derive novel generalization bounds expressed in terms of the Minimum Description Length (MDL) of the joint latent variables across all views and across both training and test datasets. Our structure-aware bound reveals that statistical correlations among the extracted representations tighten the bound, providing theoretical grounding for the empirically observed benefits

translated_title: 基于分布式联合潜在空间结构的多视图表示学习
translated_abstract: arXiv:2504.18455v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：我们研究了分布式多视图表示学习问题，其中$K$个客户端各自观察一个不同但可能统计相关的视图。客户端独立地从其视图中提取局部表示，然后由中央解码器用于联合目标估计。一个核心难点在于，由于客户端之间不允许通信，它们必须自主决定编码什么。我们从泛化误差的角度研究这一协调问题。对于分类和回归任务，我们推导出新颖的泛化界限，这些界限以所有视图以及训练和测试数据集中联合潜在变量的最小描述长度（MDL）来表示。我们的结构感知界限揭示了提取表示之间的统计相关性会收紧界限，为经验观察到的益处提供了理论基础。
tldr: 本文通过最小描述长度推导出结构感知泛化界限，证明多视图表示间的统计相关性可提升分布式学习性能，为协同编码提供了理论依据。
en_tdlr: This paper derives structure-aware generalization bounds via Minimum Description Length, showing that statistical correlations among multiview representations tighten the bounds, providing theoretical grounding for improved distributed learning performance.
